summary: The footer list of sources, as an ordered list so the count and order are structural.
useWhen: several claims cite sources and the reader should be able to see them all at once

useInstead.when: there is one source and it belongs in the sentence
it is tabular data with more than a source per row

label.note: rendered as plain text, not a heading element — it should not enter the document outline as a section

guarantees: an <ol>, so a screen reader can say how many sources there are before the reader commits to hearing them
list markers are hidden in CSS while the semantics stay, because the visible number must match the inline Citation's exactly

antiPatterns.why: the count and the ordering are the useful part, and only a list carries them

antiPatterns.dont: numbers that disagree with the inline markers
antiPatterns.why: the marker is a promise about where to look
